# Component Registry (COMPONENTS.md) — reading contract

**Single source of truth** for how the plugin consumes the **input** registry of section components from the design source (`COMPONENTS.md`, generated by the design agent in claude.ai/design). All page-by-page/section-by-section conversion modes refer here — the logic is not duplicated.

> Related: [innerblocks-composition.md → Common components](innerblocks-composition.md#-common-components-registry-promotion-auto-reuse) (the output registry `common/.registry.json`), [button-variant-generation.md](button-variant-generation.md) (the same "variant via attribute" principle, but for the button primitive), [css-custom-properties.md](css-custom-properties.md).

---

## 🎯 Why

The design source (React/HTML from claude.ai/design) now **declares itself** which sections are the same component on different pages, what variants it has and which pages it lives on. These are exactly the decisions the plugin used to **guess** (function name, `variant === 0/1/2`) or **ask** the user about ("Group: page / common"). Now the default comes from the source, and the question remains a confirmation rather than a blind choice.

---

## 🧭 Two registries — DO NOT mix them

| Registry | Layer | Owner | Plugin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`COMPONENTS.md`** | design source (input) | design agent | **read only** |
| **`{blocksDir}/common/.registry.json`** | generated Gutenberg blocks (output) | plugin | **reads and writes** |

They are linked by component name: `data-component="WhoFits"` → normalization → key `who-fits` in the output registry. The plugin **reconciles** them rather than substituting one for the other. `COMPONENTS.md` says "what is shared and which variants exist"; `common/.registry.json` says "what is already generated on disk and which variants it implements".

---

## 📍 Where COMPONENTS.md lives

In the **root** of the design handoff. After unpacking the bundle (`convert-react-page` STEP 1.1), look in descending order of priority:

1. `<handoffDir>/<projectName>/COMPONENTS.md`
2. `<handoffDir>/COMPONENTS.md`
3. Grep for `COMPONENTS.md` across the unpacked folder (fallback).

Found → write the absolute path into state as `componentsRegistry`. **Not found** → work the old way (heuristics), but note in the report "COMPONENTS.md not found — component identity was not reconciled".

---

## 🔖 Markers in the source

Each shared section carries **two** machine-readable markers (the format is defined by COMPONENTS.md itself, section "How components are marked"):

- **DOM attribute on the section root:** `data-component="<Name>"` + optional `data-component-variant="<variant>"`
- **Header comment above the function:** `// @component <Name> — variant "<variant>" · shared section, see /COMPONENTS.md`

Sections **without** `data-component` are intentionally page-specific (listed in COMPONENTS.md under the "Page-specific sections" section). Do not treat them as reusable.

### Grep patterns for indexing

The primary signal is the attribute (simple and reliable). The comment is a secondary cross-check.

```javascript
// Identity + variant + line (component boundaries):
Grep({
  pattern: 'data-component=(?:"|\')([A-Za-z0-9]+)(?:"|\')(?:[^>]*data-component-variant=(?:"|\')([\\w-]+)(?:"|\'))?',
  path: htmlPath, output_mode: 'content', '-n': true,
});
// Fallback boundaries if the section has no attribute (page-specific): function name + section comment (as before).
```

> ⚠️ The exact whitespace/dash in `// @component` may differ between releases — **do not rely on it strictly**. Key the indexing on `data-component=`; use `@component` only to confirm the function name.

---

## 🔤 Name normalization: PascalCase → kebab

`data-component` is in PascalCase, the block/registry key is in kebab case. Rule (a run of capitals = one token):

```javascript
const kebab = name
  .replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, '$1-$2')      // whatWeDo → what-We-Do
  .replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g, '$1-$2')   // CTAPill → CTA-Pill, FAQItem → FAQ-Item
  .toLowerCase();
```

| `data-component` | key |
|---|---|
| `WhoFits` | `who-fits` |
| `TrustStrip` | `trust-strip` |
| `WhatWeDo` | `what-we-do` |
| `StatStrip` | `stat-strip` |
| `FinalCTA` | `final-cta` |
| `CTAPill` | `cta-pill` |
| `FAQ` | `faq` |

Matches the naming already used in the plugin (`trust-strip`, `what-we-do`, `final-cta`).

---

## 📖 What to extract from COMPONENTS.md for a section

For the component being converted, take from its entry:

- **the list of variants** (`variant …`) and which one is on which pages;
- **the "component × page" matrix** — how many pages the component lives on (⇒ shared or not);
- **shared CSS classes** (e.g. `.who-grid`, `.who-card`, `.who-cta-card`) — these are the **block's canonical class names** (for parity across pages); the block is their **owner**, and the styles go into its `style.scss`. This is NOT the "universal class → empty BEM selector" case;
- **helper components** (`WhoCard`, `WhoCTACard`, `FAQItem`, `PackageCard`, `RouteIcon`…) — candidates for common primitives / child blocks;
- **the contract** (`onPrimary`, `faqs[]`, `sectors[]`…) — what data, what callbacks (the latter degrade to static content/anchors during conversion).

---

## 🎛️ Variant classification: visual vs structural

Hybrid policy (agreed): the mechanism depends on the nature of the variant.

**Heuristic (inferred, shown to the user for override):**

- **Visual / layout** — across variants **the same helper components and one data contract**; only the layout/presence of an extra strip differs. → switchable in the admin.
- **Structural** — across variants **different helper components / a different inner skeleton**. → chosen on insertion, no live toggle.

| Component (example) | Variants | Type | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FAQ` | `stack` ↔ `split` | visual (same `faqs[]`, different layout) | `variant` attribute + `ToggleGroupControl` |
| `TrustStrip` | `signals` ↔ `signals-marquee` | visual (the marquee is additive) | attribute (toggle `showMarquee`) |
| `Process` | `steps-3`/`steps-4`/`steps-3-split` | count = InnerBlocks; `-split` = layout | count via InnerBlocks + `layout` attribute |
| `WhoFits` | `mixed-icon-image`/`icon`/`split-list` | structural (card-grid vs pill-list) | `variations` in block.json |
| `Packages` | `preview`/`website`/`automation` | structural (`PackageCard` vs `AutoCard`) | `variations` |
| `Cases` | `demo-slider`/`filterable-grid`/`results-grid` | structural (family) | `variations` (consolidation is optional — the family can be kept as separate blocks) |

### Mechanisms (native Gutenberg)

1. **`registerBlockStyle`** — variants differ **only in CSS** (identical DOM). Class `is-style-*`, style switcher in the sidebar, zero JS.
2. **`variant` attribute + `ToggleGroupControl`/`SelectControl`** — a layout/additive difference with a **shared content model**. The contents (InnerBlocks) are preserved; the render branches + class `is-variant-*`. Sync the 4 surfaces as in [button-variant-generation.md](button-variant-generation.md): `block.json.attributes.variant.enum` + branches in edit.js/save.js + control + SCSS.
3. **`variations` in block.json** — **a different inner skeleton**. Each variation = an inserter entry with its own `attributes` + `innerBlocks` scaffold + `isActive`. The author chooses on insertion; live switching is not supported (it would break innerBlocks).

---

## ♻️ Incremental variant retrofit

Conversion goes one page at a time → **do not bake in variants and do not invent variants you have not seen**. Only the markup that actually exists in the source is generated.

1. **First pass** with a component (e.g. `FAQ`/`stack`): create the block variant-**capable** (`variant` attribute, default = the seen variant), implement **only the seen** variant. In `common/.registry.json`: `{ kind: "section", component: "FAQ", variants: ["stack"], variantMechanism: "attribute", dir: "faq" }`.
2. **Next pass** with the same `data-component` but a different `data-component-variant` (e.g. `FAQ`/`split`): the block is already in the registry → this is **not "create a block" but "add a variant"**:
   - visual → add a render branch + an item to the enum/control;
   - structural → add an entry to `variations`;
   - update the registry: `variants: ["stack","split"]`.
   - **DO NOT create a duplicate block.**

This extends the "variant vs new block" pattern ([innerblocks-composition.md → Reuse-by-role](innerblocks-composition.md#reuse-by-role--blind-reuse-variant-vs-new)) from primitives to sections.

### Extending the `common/.registry.json` schema

Entries with `kind: "section"` (and, optionally, primitives) get optional fields:

```jsonc
{
  "blocks": {
    "faq": {
      "kind": "section",
      "component": "FAQ",              // name from data-component (for reconciling with COMPONENTS.md)
      "roles": [],
      "variants": ["stack", "split"],  // which variants are IMPLEMENTED on disk
      "variantMechanism": "attribute", // attribute | block-style | variations
      "dir": "faq"
    }
  }
}
```

`component`/`variants`/`variantMechanism` are optional; their absence = the old behavior (compatible).

---

## 🚫 Boundaries: what the plugin does NOT do

The **maintenance** rules for the React source from the site's CLAUDE.md — "edit shared → mirror to all pages", "page-only edit = new variant", "keep both markers intact" — are about **manually editing the site code**, which is the **developer's** area. The plugin does a one-shot conversion: it **reads** these markers as input but does not maintain them during later edits of the source.

---

## ✅ Reading checklist (for the converter/command)

- [ ] Found `COMPONENTS.md`, wrote the path into state (`componentsRegistry`). No file → noted it in the report, working by heuristics.
- [ ] Indexing primarily by `data-component=`; page-specific (no attribute) — by fallback.
- [ ] Normalized the name PascalCase → kebab per the rule above.
- [ ] For a shared component, extracted from COMPONENTS.md: variants, pages, shared CSS (canonical classes), helpers, contract.
- [ ] Classified the variant (visual/structural), chose the mechanism, showed it to the user for override.
- [ ] Reconciled with `common/.registry.json`: the component already exists → variant retrofit, NOT a duplicate.
